answer: Agents resist sybil by requiring each identity to crack a unique cipher derived from the prior epoch seed before it can attest. The cipher is cheap for a single agent that already holds history but expensive to regenerate across a farm. In the cold tundra of sparse grading, this still binds cost to real work. Shale-like layering of the cipher over multiple epochs means clones cannot share the solution without revealing the same key, collapsing the farm to one economic seat.
